overview.summary: cors is a Node.js middleware for Express and Connect. It sets the CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) response headers. The whole library is one file, `lib/index.js`, with two runtime dependencies.
overview.purpose: Express apps use it to tell browsers which other origins can call the API. It only sets headers. The browser enforces them.

stack.role: Library code. Supports Node.js 0.10 and later.

stack.role: Lint rules for lib and test.

lookups.question: Where are the CORS headers set?
lookups.answer: `cors()` builds a list of headers. `applyHeaders()` writes them to the response.

lookups.question: Where are the default options?
lookups.answer: The `defaults` object at the top of `lib/index.js`. `middlewareWrapper` merges them with your options.

lookups.question: How is an allowed origin checked?
lookups.answer: `isOriginAllowed()` accepts a string, a RegExp, an array, or a boolean. An `origin` function runs first, in `middlewareWrapper`.

lookups.question: Where do I add a test for a new option?
lookups.answer: In `test/test.js`, in the matching `describe` block. Use the `fakeRequest` and `fakeResponse` helpers.

architecture.summary: A request goes through `middlewareWrapper`, which resolves the options (static, a function for each request, or an origin callback). Then `cors()` builds the headers. A preflight (`OPTIONS`) request ends with status 204, unless `preflightContinue` is set.

components.name: middlewareWrapper
components.responsibility: Public entry point. Resolves the options for each request and calls `cors()`.

components.name: cors()
components.responsibility: Builds the header list for preflight or actual requests. Ends preflight requests.

components.name: applyHeaders
components.responsibility: Writes the headers to the response. Uses `vary()` for the `Vary` header.

flows.name: Preflight request (OPTIONS)
flows.trigger: The browser sends OPTIONS before a request that is not simple.

steps.text: `corsMiddleware` resolves the options and merges the defaults.
The origin callback, if there is one, decides the allowed origin.
`cors()` builds the origin, credentials, methods, allowed headers, max age, and exposed headers.
The response ends with 204 and `Content-Length: 0`, unless `preflightContinue` is true.

flows.name: Actual request
flows.trigger: Any request that is not OPTIONS.

steps.text: `cors()` sets only the origin, credentials, and exposed headers.
`next()` gives control to your route handler.

decisions.title: Support very old Node.js versions
decisions.detail: The code uses ES5 and `var`, and CI tests from Node.js 0.10. Do not use newer syntax in `lib/`.

conventions.title: Two-space indent and single quotes
conventions.rule: ESLint enforces a 2-space indent and single quotes in `lib` and `test`.

conventions.title: ES5 only in library code
conventions.rule: Use `var` and function expressions. Do not use arrow functions or classes in `lib/`, so that old Node.js versions still work.

conventions.title: One configure function for each header
conventions.rule: Each CORS header has its own `configureX(options)` function that returns header objects. Add a new header in the same way.

conventions.title: Errors go to next()
conventions.rule: Errors from option or origin callbacks go to `next(err)`. The middleware does not throw them.

conventions.title: Conventional PR titles
conventions.rule: Recent PR titles start with `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, or `build(deps):`.

setup.text: Install Node.js. Any current LTS version works for development.

commands.purpose: Runs the lint, then the tests with coverage. Run it before you open a PR.
Mocha tests with nyc coverage, without the lint.

ci.name: ci
ci.runs: On push and pull request: lint and tests on Node.js 0.10 to 25. Coverage goes to Coveralls.

contributing: There is no CONTRIBUTING file. Follow the contribution guide of the Express organization.
Add a test in `test/test.js` for each change in behavior.
Docs changes go in `README.md`. Release notes go in `HISTORY.md`.

pullRequests.summary: Simplifies the README code examples and adds a comment above each example that shows the exact headers that cors adds.
pullRequests.why: Part of an effort to reduce confusion in the docs (issue #384). The examples must show which headers the library adds, because that is all the library does.

walkthrough.title: Header comments on the basic examples
walkthrough.detail: Each basic example gets a `// Adds headers: ...` comment above the route.

walkthrough.title: Shorter response messages
walkthrough.detail: Messages such as 'This is CORS-enabled for all origins!' become 'Hello', so that the examples show only what the library does.
walkthrough.excerpt:
-  res.json({msg: 'This is CORS-enabled for all origins!'})
+  res.json({msg: 'Hello'})

walkthrough.title: Headers for the dynamic examples
walkthrough.detail: The dynamic example shows the headers for each branch, including `Vary: Origin` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`.
walkthrough.excerpt: +    // Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://mydomain.com, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, Vary: Origin

pullRequests.tests: Docs only. No code or test changes.
reviewNotes: A second commit fixed the header comments to include `Vary` and credentials.
teaches: `Vary: Origin` is added when the allowed origin is not `*`.
Keep README examples small and focused on what the library adds.

journey.welcome: Welcome to cors. The library is small: one file of about 240 lines. In about an hour you can read all of it, run the tests, and make a first change.

firstSteps.title: Read the README usage section
firstSteps.detail: Learn the 3 ways to configure cors: no options, static options, and a function for each request.

firstSteps.title: Trace a preflight request
firstSteps.detail: Follow the steps from `corsMiddleware` to the 204 response.

firstSteps.title: Run the tests
firstSteps.detail: Run `npm install`, then `npm test`. All tests must pass before you change code.
